neighbours.label: talk about how kinds of people live: family, care and getting by (giving an ex-convict a job, grandparents living with grandchildren, older adults, 'part of our lives'), as opposed to technical or corporate matter
fire: Few landlords in the city will rent a single mother a flat without a guarantor.
More than a million children are being raised by an aunt or an older sister.
The centre offers hot meals and company for elderly people who have no relatives nearby.
Music has always been a big part of our lives, from lullabies to wedding songs.
Many employers still refuse to offer a deaf person a place on the shop floor.
After the factory closed, three generations of the family ended up living under one roof.
Volunteers visit every week to read to widowers who rarely leave their homes.
Caring for a disabled brother has shaped how she thinks about work and marriage.
quiet: Few printers in the office will feed a sheet of thick card without a jam.
More than a million barrels are being shipped by rail or by an older pipeline.
The plant produces steel beams and cable for bridges that have no central pier.
Copper has always been a big part of the circuit, from the coils to the contacts.
Many routers still refuse to assign a new device an address on the guest network.
After the merger closed, three divisions of the firm ended up reporting to one office.
Technicians inspect every week the pumps that rarely need new seals.
Polishing the telescope mirror has changed how the lab schedules its testing and calibration.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (2.1% of tokens reach 0.1 of max); peaks on function words (' to', ' a', ' with', ' como') in sentences about social groups and family life; the output suppresses ' personal' / ' individual' and promotes ' parent', ' operations'. Probes: ex-convict a job 0.46, grandparents with grandchildren 0.37, older adults 0.35, part of our lives 0.40; engine 0.03, corporate plan 0.07, 'vendors work like a family' 0.11. A topic-level label; near misses are technical, corporate or object-centred sentences of the same length.
